subject: english-literature
title: Marxism and the Frankfurt School
welcome_lead: Marxist criticism and the Frankfurt School read culture as ideology. Adorno, Benjamin, Eagleton — their tools sharpen any close reading.
meta_desc: English Literature: Marxist criticism and the Frankfurt School (Adorno, Benjamin, Eagleton).
final_note: Culture is never innocent. Read for the politics in the form.

concepts.def: Group of Marxist thinkers including Adorno, Horkheimer, Benjamin and Marcuse.
Adorno and Horkheimer's term for mass-produced culture that reinforces capitalism.

The system of ideas that naturalises social arrangements.
Marx's term for the way commodities mask social relations of production.
Gramsci's term for the consent-based dominance of a ruling group.

walkthroughs.body_html: Benjamin argues that photographic and cinematic reproduction destroys the aura of the original. Apply this to discussions of adaptation and authenticity.
Pop music, Hollywood and pulp fiction, for Adorno, sedate rather than enlighten. The critique is overstated, but the question — who benefits from this form? — remains useful.
Hegemony shows how dominant ideas come to seem natural. Literature can both sustain and rupture hegemonic common sense.
